sample_unit: emergency department attendances (validation week); 105,096 annual attendances

links.outcome: LLM balanced accuracy versus clinician review and clinical coding for alcohol, drug, self-harm identification
links.effect: LLM balanced accuracy matched or outperformed clinician review (alcohol 0.942 v 0.930, p=0.635; drug 0.959 v 0.791, p<0.001; self-harm 0.982 v 0.908, p=0.004); coding identified 6.0% vs reference 12.1%.
links.quote: LLM balanced accuracy matched or outperformed clinician review in all three domains (alcohol 0.942 v 0.930, p=0.635; drug 0.959 v 0.791, p<0.001; self-harm 0.982 v 0.908, p=0.004).

links.outcome: LLM performance on local historical data against adjudicated reference standard
links.effect: Validated in a week of local attendances (n=2,256) against a conflict-adjudicated reference standard; LLM balanced accuracy 0.942 to 0.982 across the three domains.
links.quote: In a validation week, the identification strategies were assessed against a conflict-adjudicated reference standard (n=2,256); the LLM was then applied to n=105,096 annual attendances at the same site.

unlisted_practices: Using a locally deployed open-source LLM on existing clinical free text to improve structured data completeness for surveillance
Comparing clinical coding accuracy against an adjudicated reference standard

screen.reason: This study evaluates the diagnostic/extraction accuracy of a locally deployed open-source LLM against clinical coding and clinician review on retrospective ED records (2,256 validation set, scaled to 105,096 annual attendances). It measures model accuracy and prevalence extraction but does not test a specific deployment safeguard/practice.
